display.text:
# Context Pack: `product-state-mirror` — Product-state SQLite mirror and storage migrate Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen). Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5. Domain: durability-core. Risk: high. Descriptive only — no defect judgments. ## 1. Purpose `internal/productstate` is a small generic KV mirror: two tables in the workspace-local SQLite file `.ultraplan/run-control.db` holding one row per `(kind, scope)` with a header JSON blob plus ordered per-item payload rows. Three product record types use it: | kind | scope | header | items | source JSON checkpoint | |---|---|---|---|---| | `study_run` | `` | RunState minus Tasks | one per task ID | `studies//.ultraplan/run-state.json` | | `sprint_flow` | `/` | FlowState minus Stages | one per stage name | `projects/

/sprints//flow-state.json` | | `sprint_execute` | `/` | ExecuteRunState minus Tasks | one per task ID | `projects/

/sprints//.run-state.json` | Authority model (as implemented): **if a row exists for a record, that row is authoritative on every load** ("row-wins"); the JSON file remains in place as a compatibility checkpoint, rewritten by save paths only at terminal/complete states. The `storage migrate` CLI imports existing files into the DB one-way and idempotently (per-record skip when a row already exists). Records never imported stay file-backed; there is no export/demote path. The DB file is shared with `internal/runcontrol` (run-journal-fencing surface), which owns its own tables in the same file. ## 2. Entrypoints and control flow ### 2.1 Store primitives (`internal/productstate/store.go`, whole package = 206 lines) - Constants/state: `DatabaseRelativePath = ".ultraplan/run-control.db"` (:19), `ErrNotFound` (:21), `Item{Key,Ordinal,Payload}` (:23), `Record{Kind,Scope,SchemaVersion,Header,Items}` (:29), process-wide cache `stores sync.Map` keyed by absolute root (:39). - `Existing(root)` (:41): stats the DB path; not-exist ⇒ `(nil, false, nil)`; other stat error ⇒ error; else `open(root)` returning `(store, err == nil, err)`. - `Ensure(root)` (:53): unconditionally `open(root)` (creates `.ultraplan/` 0700 and the DB file via the driver if absent). Sole callers: the three domain save-database helpers and `runStorage`. - `open(root)` (:55): abs-path cache lookup; DSN params `_busy_timeout=5000`, `_foreign_keys=on`, `_journal_mode=WAL`, `_synchronous=FULL`, `_txlock=immediate`; modernc.org/sqlite v1.57.0 driver; `SetMaxOpenConns(4)`; runs `createSchema` (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, :92-116) on every open — including opens reached through `Existing`; `LoadOrStore` race loser closes its duplicate handle. No `Close` method exists anywhere in the package. - Schema: `product_states(kind, scope, schema_version, header_json, header_hash, updated_at, PK(kind,scope))`; `product_state_items(kind, scope, item_key, ordinal, payload_json, payload_hash, PK(kind,scope,item_key), FK→product_states ON DELETE CASCADE)`; index `(kind,scope,ordinal)`; `updated_at` is RFC3339Nano UTC. - `Has` (:118): `SELECT 1 … WHERE kind,scope`. - `Load` (:127): two separate autocommit statements — header row first (`sql.ErrNoRows` ⇒ `ErrNotFound`), then items `ORDER BY ordinal`. No transaction wraps the pair; stored `header_hash`/`payload_hash` are not compared on read. - `Save` (:150): rejects empty Kind/Scope, `SchemaVersion < 1`, or empty Header before opening an immediate transaction (deferred rollback); sha256 of header; upsert with change-guard `WHERE header_hash <> excluded OR schema_version <> excluded` (no-op when identical); per-item upsert guarded on payload hash + ordinal; empty item key aborts mid-transaction; then collects existing item keys not present in the incoming set and DELETEs them inside the same tx (full-replace semantics for items); commit. ### 2.2 Sprint adapters (`internal/sprint/state_database.go`) - Kinds `sprintFlowStateKind="sprint_flow"`, `sprintExecuteStateKind="sprint_execute"` (:13-14); scope `sprintStateScope(s) = s.Project + "/" + s.Slug` (:17). - `loadSprintRecord` (:57): `Existing` (err or disabled ⇒ no record), `Load`, `ErrNotFound` ⇒ not-found. `loadFlowStateDatabase` (:19)/`loadExecuteStateDatabase` (:38): plain `json.Unmarshal` header into `FlowState`/`ExecuteRunState`, then each item payload into `StageState`/`ExecuteTaskRecord`, appended to `state.Stages`/`state.Tasks` in ordinal order. No `DisallowUnknownFields`, no single-value check, no v1 migration, no pre-code-context interpretation on this branch. - `saveFlowStateDatabase` (:69)/`saveExecuteStateDatabase` (:99): stamps `UpdatedAt=time.Now().UTC()`; resolves the canonical file path (containment-checked) and runs the full domain validator (`ValidateFlowState`/`ValidateExecuteRunState`) BEFORE any DB write; marshals header copy with Stages/Tasks nil'd; items keyed by stage name / task ID with slice index as ordinal; `Ensure`; `Store.Save(context.Background(), …)`. - `SprintStateInDatabase` (:129)/`FlowStateInDatabase` (:137)/`ExecuteStateInDatabase` (:140): `Existing`+`Has`. `MigrateFlowStateToDatabase`/`MigrateExecuteStateToDatabase` (:143-147) are thin aliases over the save helpers. ### 2.3 Study adapter (`internal/study/state_database.go`) - Kind `studyRunStateKind="study_run"`; scope is bare `study.Name` (:13). Root derivation `studyWorkspaceRoot(study) = filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(study.Path))` (:15) — two levels above `studies//.ultraplan/run-state.json`, i.e. the workspace root. - `loadRunStateDatabase` (:16): Existing/Load/plain Unmarshal header + TaskState items, same shape as sprint adapters. `saveRunStateDatabase` (:43): stamps UpdatedAt, `compactRunStateDiagnostics`, `ValidateRunState(state, RunStatePath(study))`, header = clone minus Tasks, items per task ID, Ensure, Save with `context.Background()`. `RunStateInDatabase` (:70); `MigrateRunStateToDatabase` (:78) aliases the saver. ### 2.4 Authority routing in the owning packages - Study (`study/state.go`): `LoadRunState` (:27) tries the DB first; found ⇒ `ValidateRunState` then return (no diagnostics compaction on this branch). Miss ⇒ read file, plain `json.Unmarshal` (malformed ⇒ `ErrRunStateMalformed`), validate, compact diagnostics, oversized-content GC guard (:52-55). `SaveRunState` (:59): `RunStateInDatabase` true ⇒ `saveRunStateDatabase`; file rewrite follows ONLY when `state.Complete` (:66-68); otherwise return after DB write. No row yet ⇒ file-only atomic write (temp+fsync+rename, :73-110+). - Sprint flow (`sprint/state.go`): `LoadFlowState` (:20) DB-first; found ⇒ containment-resolve path, `ValidateFlowState`, return — the file branch's v1→v2 migration and pre-code-context interpretation do NOT apply to DB records. Miss ⇒ strict file grammar (version ∈ {1,2}, DisallowUnknownFields, single JSON value; v1 migrated in memory only). `SaveFlowState`: evidence-preservation backfill of nil Review/Smoke/QA from prior state happens FIRST (:205-218), then routing (:219-230): row exists ⇒ DB save; file checkpoint written additionally only when `flowStateCheckpoint(state)` — every stage terminal (complete/failed/skipped) and non-empty (:233-240); no row ⇒ file-only. - Sprint execute (`sprint/execute_state.go`): `LoadExecuteRunState` (:35) DB-first with `ValidateExecuteRunState` on the DB branch; file branch plain Unmarshal + validate. `SaveExecuteRunState` (:105): row exists ⇒ DB save; file checkpoint only when `executeStateCheckpoint(state)` — non-empty and all tasks terminal (:120-130); else file-only. - Net effect: once a row exists, loads never consult the file again; saves update both authorities but keep the FILE stale during non-terminal transitions (checkpoint-gated). ### 2.5 `storage migrate` CLI (`internal/app/storage_commands.go`, dispatched from `app/app.go:159-160`) - Arg grammar (:33-54): no args/`--help`/`-h` ⇒ help text; subcommand must be `migrate` (else ExitUsage=2); flags `--dry-run`, `--json`, `--help/-h`; anything else ⇒ ExitUsage. - Unless dry-run (:59-68): `runcontrol.OpenSQLite(ctx, root.Path, SQLiteOptions{})` — creates `.ultraplan/` 0700, DB file 0600 O_EXCL with symlink/regular-file checks, verifies pragmas, may run runcontrol schema migration with timestamped backups; then `productstate.Ensure` adds the product tables. Errors ⇒ classified ExitWorkspace=4. Dry-run performs neither step (but see §7: existence probes still touch an already-present DB). - Result accumulation (:69-80): `storageMigrationResult{SchemaVersion: 1, DryRun, Imported/Skipped/Failed counts, Items}`; statuses `imported`/`would_import`/`skipped`/`failed`. - Study pass (:81-107): `DiscoverStudies` (name-sorted) ⇒ hard ExitWorkspace error on failure. Per study: stat `run-state.json` — not-exist ⇒ silent continue; other error ⇒ failed item. `study.RunStateInDatabase` — error ⇒ failed item; true ⇒ skipped. Else `study.LoadRunState(item)` (full validation; DB miss guaranteed since row absent); when load OK and not dry-run ⇒ `MigrateRunStateToDatabase`; append imported/would_import/failed accordingly. - Sprint pass (:108-121): `DiscoverProjects` (name-sorted) ⇒ hard ExitWorkspace error; discovery failure per project ⇒ failed project-kind item, continue; `migrateSprintState` per sprint (slug-sorted): - flow (:144-162): `FlowStatePath` resolution failure ⇒ block silently skipped; stat not-exist ⇒ silent skip; other stat error ⇒ failed. `FlowStateInDatabase` err/true ⇒ failed/skipped. Else `LoadFlowState` (strict file grammar incl. in-memory v1 migration), import via `MigrateFlowStateToDatabase` unless dry-run. - execute (:163-185): same path/stat pattern; NEW: `LegacyTerminalExecuteStatus(root, sp)` legacy ⇒ skipped item and early return (added post-feature, commit 8ee9d9c "Skip legacy terminal sprint state during migration"); otherwise `ExecuteStateInDatabase` gate then `LoadExecuteRunState` + `MigrateExecuteStateToDatabase`. - Output (:122-135): `--json` ⇒ single encoded result object; text mode prints aligned status/kind/scope/path (+error) lines and a summary line. Any failed item ⇒ classified ExitPartial=8 ("state artifact(s) failed validation or import") after full output (:136-138). - Per-record commit granularity: each import is an independent `Store.Save` transaction; there is no overall migration transaction. Re-running skips already-imported records (idempotent). Files are never modified or deleted by the command. ## 3. Inputs / outputs Inputs: workspace tree (the three JSON state files, project/study/sprint directory layout), DB file presence and rows, wall clock (`time.Now().UTC()` stamped at every DB save), CLI args (`--workspace` via `discoverWorkspace`, `--dry-run`, `--json`). Outputs: rows in `product_states`/`product_state_items` (created/updated/deleted-items within transactions), creation of `.ultraplan/run-control.db` (+WAL/SHM sidecar files) when absent via Ensure/OpenSQLite, terminal-checkpoint rewrites of source JSON files by save paths (owned by the flow/execute/study surfaces, not this pack), stdout report + exit class (0 / 2 usage / 4 workspace / 8 partial), sentinel `productstate.ErrNotFound`. ## 4. Authoritative state - Tables `product_states` and `product_state_items` inside `.ultraplan/run-control.db`, coexisting with runcontrol's own tables (`app_schema`, `runs`, `events`, `attempts`, `operation_aliases`, `reconciliation_log`, …) in the SAME file. Two independent `database/sql` pools address it: productstate (cached per absolute root, ≤4 conns, never closed) and runcontrol (per OpenSQLite call, default 4/max 16). Both use WAL + synchronous FULL + immediate txlock + busy_timeout 5000ms. - Column roles: `header_json`/`payload_json` carry state; `schema_version` mirrors the domain schema version (flow 2, execute 1, study 1) and participates in the header change-guard; `header_hash`/`payload_hash` (sha256) exist for the upsert WHERE guards only — no code path reads them back or verifies them against payloads; `updated_at` written (RFC3339Nano UTC, stamp time of the save/import, NOT inherited from the file's UpdatedAt) and never read. - Item identity: stage enum name (flow), task ID (execute/study); ordinals are slice positions at save time; deleted stages/tasks are removed from the DB by Save's stale-key sweep. - Authority decision inputs, exhaustively: DB file exists (stat) AND row exists for `(kind, scope)` ⇒ DB authoritative for that record. Everything else stays file-backed. There is no config flag, marker table, or version gate involved in the flip. - The file remains a live artifact for migrated records only at terminal states (checkpoint writes); mid-flight transitions leave the file at its last terminal snapshot while the DB advances. ## 5. Invariants (as implemented) - Domain validation precedes persistence: every DB write path runs the same validator used for files (`ValidateRunState`/`ValidateFlowState`/`ValidateExecuteRunState`) against the contained canonical path, so DB rows satisfy the same grammar as validated files at write time. - Record sanity at the store boundary: non-empty kind/scope/header, `SchemaVersion ≥ 1`, non-empty item keys; violations reject the whole Save transaction. - Atomicity: each Save is one immediate transaction covering header upsert, all item upserts, and stale-item deletions; readers see pre- or post-state per SQLite isolation. - Change-guarded writes: byte-identical headers/payloads (same hash + version/ordinal) perform no UPDATE (hash-guarded upserts), so repeated saves do not churn `updated_at`. - Full-replace item semantics: Save's final sweep deletes any stored item key absent from the incoming set, mirroring file-overwrite semantics. - Reconstruction invariant: Load appends items strictly in `ordinal` order, so reassembled Stages/Tasks order matches the saving slice order. - Row-wins authority: Load paths consult the DB first and short-circuit; Save paths route by `*InDatabase` probes. A record cannot be DB-authoritative for reads and file-authoritative for writes simultaneously. - One-way migration: import validates with existing validators, never mutates or removes source files, and skips records already present; invalid files produce failed items plus partial exit without any mutation. - Checkpoint gating: DB-authoritative saves rewrite files only under per-type terminal predicates (`Complete` for study; all-stages-terminal for flow; all-tasks-terminal & non-empty for execute). ## 6. Trust boundaries - Stored rows re-enter as authoritative product state with unconditional row-wins on read: whatever process can write the DB file can silently redirect every subsequent load/gate decision for that record. The DB file sits in the same workspace-private directory as the JSON checkpoints (`.ultraplan/` 0700, DB 0600 when created through runcontrol's `preparePrivateDatabase`), so the trust transition assumes workspace-local attacker equivalence — same actor who could edit the JSON files directly. - Decode asymmetry: DB-branch loads use plain `json.Unmarshal` for all three types (unknown fields tolerated, multiple/trailing values unchecked), whereas the sprint-flow FILE branch enforces DisallowUnknownFields + single-value grammar. Domain validators still run after DB loads (study/state.go:31, sprint/state.go:28, execute_state.go:43). - Import trust: `storage migrate` trusts file content only after the existing validators accept it; validation failures are surfaced per-item, not fatal to the run. - Integrity columns are decorative at read time: `header_hash`/`payload_hash` are never rechecked against stored blobs by any reader. - Cancellation plumbing: every store call site passes `context.Background()` (study/state_database.go:67, sprint/state_database.go:96,126, and inside store Has/Load callers) — operation contexts (web shutdown, run cancellation) do not propagate into these queries; only `runcontrol.OpenSQLite` receives the real ctx from `runStorage`. - Permission enforcement is asymmetric between pools: runcontrol Lstat-checks for symlinks/non-regular files and chmods dir+file to 0700/0600; productstate's `open` does MkdirAll(0700) and lets the SQLite driver create the file with the process umask, with no symlink/mode verification on the Existing path. ## 7. External effects & lifecycle semantics - Effects confined to the workspace DB file and (via owning packages) terminal checkpoint files. First `Ensure`/`OpenSQLite` creates `.ultraplan/run-control.db` plus `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars; productstate adds only its two tables/indexes (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), also executed on opens through `Existing` of an existing file. - Process lifecycle: stores are cached per absolute root for the life of the process and hold up to 4 open connections each; nothing closes them (no Close API). Multiple UltraPlan processes share the file through WAL + busy_timeout(5s) + immediate transactions. - Crash/restart story: committed imports persist (WAL, FULL sync); a crash mid-migration leaves a prefix of records imported — rerunning skips those (documented incremental behavior). No fencing token or lease of its own; mutual exclusion with runcontrol writers is purely SQLite locking. - Retention/backup interplay (run-journal-fencing owns these): retention compaction (`PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)`, `incremental_vacuum`) and quota enforcement operate on the whole file including product tables; runcontrol schema migrations create bounded timestamped `run-control.db.bak.*` copies (max 3 × 512 MiB) that contain product rows; `RestoreBackup` swaps the entire file, so restored snapshots revert product-state rows wholesale. - Cancellation/retry: `runStorage` has no ctx checks between per-record imports (discovery loops are sequential; store calls use Background ctx); retrying the command after partial failure is the recovery mechanism. Dry-run reports would_import/skip/failed based on current DB contents without creating the DB. - Error surfacing: infrastructural failures (workspace discovery, OpenSQLite, Ensure, DiscoverStudies/Projects) abort with ExitWorkspace before/without output items; per-record failures accumulate into the report and yield ExitPartial while remaining records still import. ## 8. Immediate surface dependencies - `run-journal-fencing` (critical, durability-core): same DB file; `runStorage` calls `runcontrol.OpenSQLite` for its create/migrate/verify side effects even though the repository value is unused beyond Close; backup/restore/quota machinery treats product tables as opaque bytes of the file. Contracts (CURRENT-CONTRACT evidence) In-repo docs (target repo): - `docs/migration-product-state.md` (added with the feature): "UltraPlan can store mutable study and sprint execution state in the workspace database instead of rewriting complete JSON documents"; preview/import via `scripts/migrate-product-state.sh [--dry-run]` (thin wrapper exec'ing `ultraplan --workspace storage migrate "$@"`); "It validates each file with the existing product validator before importing it. Existing JSON files stay in place as compatibility checkpoints. The implemented mirror is an explicit dual-home (DB authoritative + gated file checkpoints), documented in `migration-product-state.md`. - TRD.md L57/L126 treat "SQLite product persistence"/"any later SQLite authority" as requiring explicit product-mode decisions — context for the implemented-vs-planned contrast above. HISTORY: introduced wholesale in commit `02e2ec4e93bd` "Move mutable product state to SQLite" (2026-08-21, four days before freeze; 10 files, +766 lines, includes the doc and script); one follow-up `8ee9d9c` "Skip legacy terminal sprint state during migration" (+4 lines in storage_commands.go). Tests (evidence map) - `internal/productstate/` contains exactly one file (`store.go`) and **no test file**. - Repo-wide search at the frozen commit finds **zero test references** to: `productstate`, `Ensure(`, any `*InDatabase` helper, `MigrateRunStateToDatabase`/`MigrateFlowStateToDatabase`/`MigrateExecuteStateToDatabase`, `runStorage`, or the string `storage migrate`. Read-consistency scope of `Store.Load`: header query and items query run as separate autocommit statements with no transaction; whether a concurrent committed Save between them can yield a header/items mix (e.g. stale header with new item set, or partially observed delete-sweep results) depends on SQLite per-statement snapshot semantics — unstated anywhere. 2. Whether plain-Unmarshal decoding of DB payloads (unknown-field tolerant, unlike the flow file branch) is deliberate leniency for forward compatibility or incidental; DB rows also bypass the v1/pre-code-context interpretation layers entirely. 3. Intent of the integrity columns: `header_hash`/`payload_hash` are written and used as upsert guards but never verified on read; whether corruption detection was intended is undocumented. 4. Cancellation posture: all store operations use `context.Background()`; long migrations and blocked writes (busy_timeout window) ignore caller cancellation. Whether shutdown paths rely on process exit instead is unstated. 5. Permission/symlink asymmetry: a DB created by `productstate.Ensure` alone (before any runcontrol Open) gets driver-default file permissions and no symlink/mode verification, unlike runcontrol's enforced 0600/regular-file contract on the same path. 6. Pool/lifetime model: per-root store cache never closes connections and caps at 4; combined with runcontrol's own pool on the same file, worst-case concurrent connection count and busy-timeout behavior under the web server's concurrency are uncharacterized. 7. Migrate edge behavior: path-resolution failures for a sprint (FlowStatePath/ExecuteRunStatePath errors) emit NO report item at all; stat not-exist is likewise silent — whether the report should distinguish "nothing to import" from "could not inspect" is unspecified. 8. Descriptive only; no defect claims made or implied.

package study

import "time"

type TaskStatus string

const (
	TaskStatusPending    TaskStatus = "pending"
	TaskStatusRunning    TaskStatus = "running"
	TaskStatusValidating TaskStatus = "validating"
	TaskStatusCompleted  TaskStatus = "completed"
	TaskStatusFailed     TaskStatus = "failed"
	TaskStatusCancelled  TaskStatus = "cancelled"
	TaskStatusSkipped    TaskStatus = "skipped"
	TaskStatusWaiting    TaskStatus = "waiting"
	TaskStatusRetrying   TaskStatus = "retrying"
)

type RunState struct {
	SchemaVersion            int           `json:"schema_version"`
	RunID                    string        `json:"run_id"`
	Study                    string        `json:"study"`
	CreatedAt                time.Time     `json:"created_at"`
	UpdatedAt                time.Time     `json:"updated_at"`
	Filters                  RunFilters    `json:"filters"`
	Config                   ConfigSummary `json:"config_summary"`
	ApplicabilityFingerprint string        `json:"applicability_fingerprint,omitempty"`
	Tasks                    []TaskState   `json:"tasks"`
	Complete                 bool          `json:"complete"`
}

type RunFilters struct {
	Dimensions []string `json:"dimensions,omitempty"`
	Sources    []string `json:"sources,omitempty"`
}

type ConfigSummary struct {
	Runtime          string `json:"runtime,omitempty"`
	Model            string `json:"model,omitempty"`
	Variant          string `json:"variant,omitempty"`
	DefaultParallel  int    `json:"default_parallel,omitempty"`
	DefaultTimeout   string `json:"default_timeout,omitempty"`
	DefaultRetries   int    `json:"default_retries,omitempty"`
	WorkspaceVersion string `json:"workspace_version,omitempty"`
}

type TaskState struct {
	ID           string                `json:"id"`
	Kind         TaskKind              `json:"kind"`
	Status       TaskStatus            `json:"status"`
	Study        string                `json:"study"`
	Dimension    string                `json:"dimension,omitempty"`
	DimensionRef string                `json:"dimension_ref,omitempty"`
	Source       string                `json:"source,omitempty"`
	SourceKind   SourceKind            `json:"source_kind,omitempty"`
	OutputPath   string                `json:"output_path"`
	Attempts     int                   `json:"attempts"`
	CreatedAt    time.Time             `json:"created_at"`
	UpdatedAt    time.Time             `json:"updated_at"`
	StartedAt    *time.Time            `json:"started_at,omitempty"`
	CompletedAt  *time.Time            `json:"completed_at,omitempty"`
	RetryAfter   *time.Time            `json:"retry_after,omitempty"`
	LastError    *TaskError            `json:"last_error,omitempty"`
	Validation   *ValidationSummary    `json:"validation,omitempty"`
	Agent        AgentMetadata         `json:"agent,omitempty"`
	Session      *TaskSession          `json:"session,omitempty"`
	Dependencies []SynthesisDependency `json:"dependencies,omitempty"`
}

// TaskSession is the durable checkpoint needed to continue interrupted study
// work without attaching a different task or a changed prompt to the session.
type TaskSession struct {
	SessionID        string    `json:"session_id"`
	Provider         string    `json:"provider,omitempty"`
	Model            string    `json:"model,omitempty"`
	WorkDir          string    `json:"work_dir"`
	InputFingerprint string    `json:"input_fingerprint"`
	UpdatedAt        time.Time `json:"updated_at"`
	ContinueFailures int       `json:"continue_failures,omitempty"`
}

type TaskError struct {
	Code    string `json:"code,omitempty"`
	Message string `json:"message"`
	Detail  string `json:"detail,omitempty"`
	Path    string `json:"path,omitempty"`
}

type ValidationSummary struct {
	Status       ValidationStatus `json:"status"`
	CheckedAt    time.Time        `json:"checked_at"`
	Path         string           `json:"path"`
	PassedChecks int              `json:"passed_checks"`
	FailedChecks int              `json:"failed_checks"`
	Message      string           `json:"message,omitempty"`
}

type SynthesisDependency struct {
	TaskID     string     `json:"task_id"`
	Source     string     `json:"source"`
	SourceKind SourceKind `json:"source_kind"`
	ReportPath string     `json:"report_path"`
}

type StatusSummary struct {
	Total       int
	Pending     int
	Running     int
	Validating  int
	Completed   int
	Failed      int
	Cancelled   int
	Skipped     int
	Waiting     int
	Retrying    int
	Active      int
	RetryCount  int
	NextRetryAt *time.Time
	Complete    bool
	StatePath   string

	ErrExecuteRunStateMissing     = errors.New("execute run state missing")
	ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed   = errors.New("execute run state malformed")

)

type Sprint struct {
	Project string
	Slug    string
	Path    string
}

type PlanningStage string

const (
	StageRequirements      PlanningStage = "requirements"
	StageCodeContext       PlanningStage = "code-context"
	StageSprintIndex       PlanningStage = "sprint-index"
	StageTechnicalHandbook PlanningStage = "technical-handbook"
	StageAreaReasoning     PlanningStage = "area-reasoning"
	StageReasoning         PlanningStage = "reasoning"
	StagePlan              PlanningStage = "plan"
)

The tear is demonstrated: reader's reassembled record = header snapshot 1 (`complete:false`, run_id etc. from T1) + items snapshot 2 (task-2 deleted at T2). `Store.Load` produces a state that never existed atomically in the DB.

Concrete downstream consequence for study: `LoadRunState` returns this mixed state (it passes `ValidateRunState` — nothing checks task-set coherence against header). Consumers: study status/resume logic reads `state.Complete` and `state.Tasks`. E.g., a resume/status command during concurrent activity sees complete=false with a task set that's missing rows deleted by a concurrent save... wait — when does a Save DELETE items? Actually, wait — I should double check how reachable item-SET changes are:

So set-changing saves are real for studies (task append), plus payload-only updates everywhere (very frequent). Payload-only saves still tear header-vs-items (e.g., old UpdatedAt/Complete with new statuses).

Also relevant frequency context: multi-process concurrency is explicitly supported (WAL + busy_timeout + immediate txlock designed for CLI+server sharing). A `study status` CLI while web server runs the loop would hit this window routinely on every save.

Counter-evidence check: does anything downstream REQUIRE atomic consistency such that tear causes wrong behavior? The state returned is "valid but from two points in time". For gates like "don't rerun completed review", decisions use Review pointer from header + stage statuses from items — cross-time mixing could produce e.g. header.Review.LastComplete fingerprint matched against OLD stage statuses... speculative. The core defect: non-atomic multi-statement read of a record whose writers guarantee per-record atomicity (single tx). Invariant stated in context pack §5: "readers see pre- or post-state per SQLite isolation" — that claim is FALSE as implemented; readers can see a MIX. So it violates the surface's own documented invariant. That's a solid finding: invariant violation, mechanism proven empirically, code evidence store.go:127-148.

Existing() called repeatedly returns cached store after first open! Look at open(): cache lookup first → cached ⇒ no createSchema. So only first access pays. NON-ISSUE for steady state. But productstate stores live in EVERY process that touched loads (web server!). If an operator restores while server is stopped, next server start reopens fresh — fine. display.text:
# Product-state SQLite migration

UltraPlan can store mutable study and sprint execution state in the workspace
database instead of rewriting complete JSON documents after each transition.

Preview the migration:

```sh
scripts/migrate-product-state.sh /path/to/workspace --dry-run
```

Import every valid state artifact:

```sh
scripts/migrate-product-state.sh /path/to/workspace
```

The command discovers study `run-state.json`, sprint `flow-state.json`, and
sprint `.run-state.json` files. It validates each file with the existing product
validator before importing it. Invalid files remain unchanged and produce a
partial-failure exit status. Re-running the command skips records already in the
database.

After import, SQLite is authoritative for that record. Existing JSON files stay
in place as compatibility checkpoints. Unmigrated records remain file-backed,
so migration can be performed incrementally.

The normalized tables are `product_states` and `product_state_items`. Study
tasks, sprint stages, and sprint execute tasks occupy separate ordered rows.
Large generated reports, prompts, and diagnostics remain files.

part.text: All experiments done. Checking the gauntlet's artifact conventions before writing findings:

reasoning_details.text:
The doc calls --dry-run a "Preview the migration". Universal meaning of preview/dry-run: no changes. The empirical demonstration (product tables created in an existing DB during dry-run) violates that expectation, though the write is schema-only and idempotent.

Now let me finalize the counter-evidence sweep on the two remaining "maybe" items and then also quickly scan `runStorage`'s study loop for one more subtle thing I noticed:

```go
state, err := study.LoadRunState(item)
if err == nil && !dryRun {
    err = study.MigrateRunStateToDatabase(item, state)
}
appendItem(migrationItem("study_run", item.Name, path, dryRun, err))
```

`LoadRunState` on DB-miss reads file AND COMPACTS diagnostics in memory. Import persists compacted state — fine (documented durable form).

But notice: **`MigrateRunStateToDatabase` re-stamps UpdatedAt=time.Now()** — imported row's updated_at ≠ file's updated_at. Provenance loss noted in pack unknown #8; cosmetic here.

One more: **migrate imports state loaded with LoadRunState which includes GC-guard... irrelevant.

And: **the sprint flow import path uses `sprint.LoadFlowState(root, sp)` which performs v1→v2 migration + pre-code-context interpretation IN MEMORY then imports the transformed state** while the FILE stays v1/5-stage. If migrate crashes after flow import but before execute import → rerun skips flow (row exists), imports execute. Fine. But now the v1 FILE remains and is permanently shadowed. Documented one-way semantics. Fine.

**Last sweep — anything wrong in how `runStorage` handles `--json` encode failure mid-stream? Cosmetic.

**Also check**: `storage migrate` when `.ultraplan/run-control.db` exists as DIRECTORY (weird): Existing stat ok (dir!) → open → sql.Open lazy + createSchema Exec fails ("unable to open database file" or "file is not a database") → err → RunStateInDatabase error → failed items per record → ExitPartial. Reasonable-ish surface behavior (per-item failures rather than clean workspace-class error). Edge case, acceptable. Non-issue.

**Check `Existing` when DB file exists but is NOT a SQLite DB (garbage bytes)**: same as above → every record fails → ExitPartial 8 with N failed items. Noisy but honest. Hmm — actually wait: createSchema failure inside open() returns err from Existing → loadSprintRecord returns (Record{}, false, err) → LoadFlowState returns error → migrateSprintState: FlowStateInDatabase errors → failed item per artifact. So a corrupt DB yields up to 2N failed items + exit 8 instead of a single clear "database unreadable" ExitWorkspace. Report-quality issue only. Skip.

Now — final review of candidate list and severities. Let me also do one LAST careful read of Save() for any missed real bug...

```go
if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO product_states...
WHERE product_states.header_hash <> excluded.header_hash OR product_states.schema_version <> excluded.schema_version`, ...)
```

Hmm — ONE MORE THING. The header change-guard omits comparison of header_json itself; relies on sha256 collision resistance. Fine.

Items guard: `payload_hash <> excluded.payload_hash OR ordinal <> excluded.ordinal`. Same.

**Sweep query runs INSIDE tx after upserts — sees own writes. Correct.

**DELETE loop sequential — fine.

**Commit — deferred Rollback no-ops after commit (returns nil error). Fine.

What about **ctx cancellation mid-Save via context.Background()** — never cancels. By design here.

**One more genuinely-new check: `Store.Save` does not validate that Items' Ordinals are unique/contiguous** — internally generated; external writers could write ties; Load ORDER BY ordinal with ties → unspecified order → for flow, ValidateFlowState order check fails (fail-closed); for study, tasks could reorder silently (no order requirement) → e.g., dependencies referencing by ID unaffected. Only reachable via direct DB writes = outside trust model. Dismissed.

DONE with investigation. Final findings list:

**Finding 1 (medium severity, high confidence): Store.Load reads are not atomic — header and items come from different snapshots under concurrent saves, violating the surface's stated pre/post-state invariant.**

- Trigger: any concurrent Save committing between the two statements — multi-process use is an explicit design target (WAL/busy_timeout/immediate DSN).
- Bad outcome: LoadRunState/LoadFlowState/LoadExecuteRunState return records that never existed atomically; for studies this passes validation silently (no cross-check between header and task set), feeding mixed state to status/resume/gate decisions; for flow/execute count-changing saves produce spurious validation failures.

- Regression test: integration test with two connections interleaving a commit between Load's statements (deterministic via pre-commit hook or repeated timing loop asserting header/items consistency).

**Finding 2 (low-medium, high confidence): `storage migrate --dry-run` mutates an existing workspace database's schema.**
- storage_commands.go:59-68 skips Ensure/OpenSQLite when dry-run, BUT probes call productstate.Existing→open→createSchema (store.go:79 executes DDL) which CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS-writes product tables into a runcontrol-only DB. Demonstrated: dropped tables, ran dry-run, tables reappeared. Also takes schema write locks / creates WAL sidecars against a possibly-live DB.
- Misleading success angle: a "preview" performs DDL on production data; under contention it can even fail with SQLITE_BUSY surfacing as per-item "failed" (ExitPartial) despite being dry-run.
- Nuance: identical side effect occurs on ANY first load in any command, so it's systemic leniency of Existing(); but migrate --dry-run is the one place where the contract explicitly promises observation-only.

**Finding 3 (low, high confidence): dry-run text summary reports would-imports as "imported".**
- appendItem counts "would_import" into result.Imported (storage_commands.go:73-74); text summary prints "%d imported" (:134). Demonstrated: "--dry-run → Product-state migration: 3 imported, 0 skipped, 0 failed".

**Finding 4 (low-medium confidence-of-defect vs design, high confidence mechanism): corrupted/incoherent authoritative row hard-bricks the record with no recovery path through shipped commands; valid checkpoint ignored.**

- This is the documented authority model taken to its consequence; report as durability gap with concrete reproduction, noting it's partly by-design (fail-closed) but lacks any documented remediation.

Hmm, is Finding 4 within doctrine? "Do not report architecture concerns unless they create concrete failure." Concrete failure demonstrated (command unusable until manual sqlite surgery). Trigger requires corruption/mismatch event though — externally induced. It borders on "hypothetical". The strongest framing is the COMBINATION: authority flip has no integrity verification (hashes present but unchecked) + no repair path + fail-closed loads. I'll include it as a lower-severity finding with honest preconditioning, since the surface owns both the skip-on-row logic and the unchecked hashes.

Actually — let me reconsider whether there's a REALISTIC trigger for finding 4 beyond manual tampering: RestoreBackup swaps whole file (offline, documented) → rows revert wholesale; if post-restore file checkpoints are NEWER than restored rows... file still loses (row-wins). Scenario: server ran for weeks post-backup with DB authority; file checkpoint frozen at some terminal state; restore rolls DB back to backup-time rows → all progress since backup LOST from authority's perspective while newer file checkpoints exist but are ignored. Recovery = none documented (migrate skips). That's a REAL operational trap combining supported features (restore is a shipped operation; checkpoint gating guarantees files lag). But restore-reverts-everything is inherent to restore semantics and belongs primarily to run-journal-fencing. I'll mention within finding 4 as aggravating context, primary ownership noted.

**Defended non-issues** (report briefly):
- Silent skip when FlowStatePath fails: unreachable for discovered sprints (lexical containment always holds; discovery filters hidden/unsafe names).
- Permissions of Ensure-created DB: empirically 0600 even umask 022 (driver default), matching runcontrol's enforcement.
- Special chars/spaces in workspace path in DSN: works (percent-decoding verified end-to-end).
- Duplicate item keys collapse at store level: unreachable — all three savers run domain validators rejecting duplicates before Save.
- Hash-guard skipping updated_at bump when only ordinals/items change: cosmetic only, no consumer reads updated_at.
- v1/pre-code-context interpretation bypass on DB branch: DB can only contain v2 (all savers validate current version); import path migrates in memory first.

- Per-record commit granularity/no global tx in migrate: matches documented incremental retry story.

My earlier statement "count-changing saves produce spurious failures" applies only if item sets changed — which happens for STUDY (task append) and never for flow/execute. Let me correct: for flow/execute the tear = header fields (UpdatedAt, Review pointer etc.) vs items from another instant — passes validation, mixed snapshot served. Tear direction is always header(older)+items(newer). Good — precise.

So concrete worst case: study resume/status observes complete=false (old) with tasks already terminal (new) → benign-looking; or synthesis-task appended in items while header (old) lacks... header doesn't enumerate tasks. Verified at frozen commits (`50d6f0d2` / workspace `ab12dc38`). Baseline `go test ./internal/app` green. Two probes were run via `go test -overlay` with files outside the repo — **no target file was created or modified by me**. ## Findings

### F1 — TUI reruns of identical operations are blocked until retention expiry (~37 days) — Severity: HIGH, Confidence: HIGH (probe-proven)
`tui/app.go:236-238` derives the accept digest as `sha256(CanonicalRequest + "\x00" + InputFingerprint)` — no nonce, session, or token. `AcceptOperation` maps an alias PK conflict to `Existing:true` (`durable_operations.go:106-112`; alias insert `runcontrol/sqlite.go:445-455`), and aliases are only removed by FK cascade when the run row is deleted — i.e., after `FullHistory+TombstoneHistory` = 7d+30d default (`retention.go:142-150`, `model.go:423-424`, schema `sqlite.go:306-314`; `expires_at` is never written; `Compact` never touches aliases; `ResolveOperationAlias` has no terminal filter).
Observable bad outcome (probe): accept → finish(failed) → re-accept the same request returns `Existing=true`, lifecycle `failed` — the TUI shows the static "matching durable operation already exists" card and cannot start. Since governed inputs for smoke/review/execute exclude their mutable artifacts (`operations.go:663-686`), fingerprints repeat verbatim between attempts, so routine smoke retries, review reruns, and auto-next executes are locked out of the TUI. The web adapter does not have this problem (`confirmationDedupKey` includes the one-time preparation token, `security.go:396-451`), QA ops self-unblock via hashed `.run-state.json`. Violates CURRENT-CONTRACT rerun parity (TRD L2079, L436) and sprint-32's retry-safe-per-short-lived-confirmation intent.
Regression test: accept→finish→accept same digest must yield a new run; fix = include a per-preparation nonce in the TUI digest (mirroring web).

### F2 — User cancellation of an inner runtime run is durably recorded as `persistence_degraded` — Severity: MEDIUM-HIGH, Confidence: HIGH (probe-proven)
The trailing coalesced-omission flush runs on the already-cancelled `runCtx` (`run_control.go:302-316`) instead of a detached bounded context; its failure unconditionally becomes `persistenceErr`, which skips `terminalOutcome` and proposes `TerminalPersistenceLost` (`run_control.go:322-331`; `Append` returns `ctx.Err()` at `sqlite.go:639-645`).
Probe: two identical tool-progress events 250ms-window-coalesced, parent cancelled → journal terminal `persistence_degraded` / "durable event persistence failed", returned error `persist progress omission: context canceled`. Routine Ctrl-C/deadline/durable-cancellation with pending omissions therefore pollutes the persistence-failure signal, misleads operators, and contradicts the outer tier which records `cancelled` for the same user action. Trigger is common (bursty tool-part updates within the 250ms window then cancellation).
Regression test: probe above must yield `TerminalCancelled`.

### F3 — Outer tier never records persistence loss mid-run; tick failures vanish silently — Severity: MEDIUM, Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH
`ownedDurableOperation` has no persistence tracking (`durable_operations.go:21-32`): `RecordOperationEvent` append failure just calls `owned.cancel()` (:208-216), and every `controlOperation` tick failure cancels and exits without surfacing or persisting anything (:235-261). `FinishOperation`'s mapping (:286-297) has no persistence branch, so such runs terminalize as `cancelled`/`failed` — never `persistence_degraded` — in contrast to the inner tier in the same package (`run_control.go:196-203,322-331`). Concretely reachable under hard-quota pressure, where non-reserved progress appends fail while reserved terminal/warning writes still succeed (`sqlite.go:620,713-720`): journal says "operation cancelled", truth is "storage full". Also contradicts the surface invariant that persistence loss ends in a `persistence_lost` terminal.
Regression test: fault-injected Append after start must produce `TerminalPersistenceLost` (or at minimum a persisted warning); today it produces `cancelled`.

### F4 — Web/TUI operation cancellation bypasses durable cancellation recording — Severity: LOW-MEDIUM, Confidence: HIGH (code)
Hub cancel only fires the local context cancel (`web/operations.go:347-374`); same for TUI (`tui/app.go:256`, copy at :265 claims "durable cancellation"). No `RequestCancellation` row/event is written for hub-owned operations, so `cancellation_state` stays `none`, no ownerless cancellation/ack events exist, and cross-process observers see the run active until the abrupt finish. TRD requires cancellation be "idempotent, durably recorded … arbitrated". The durable path exists (`app/run_commands.go:216`; handler fallback `operation_handlers.go:206-213`) but is reached only when the hub record is absent.

### F5 — Hub mutex held across acceptance I/O stalls all operations — Severity: LOW-MEDIUM, Confidence: MEDIUM
`startConfirmed` holds `h.mu` across token consume + `AcceptOperation` — including claim and the first append with its ≤5s Busy/Unavailable retry loop (`web/operations.go:151-218`; `run_control.go:345-356`). A slow or contended database (multi-process same-workspace access is a supported TRD scenario; busy_timeout is 5s) freezes `status`, `subscribe`, SSE fan-out, and every other start for the whole process.

### F6 — Promoted display keys can never persist; every message event gains a misleading "unsafe" omission — Severity: LOW, Confidence: HIGH (code)
`runtimeEventDraft` promotes `text/delta/content/title/native_type/line` "that the run timeline JS expects" (`run_control.go:450-453,478,521-529`), but the storage allowlist omits exactly those keys (`sanitize.go:10-21,36-50`), dropping them and tagging each event `unsafe event detail omitted`. Assistant/tool text is thus never durable despite the pipeline's stated purpose, and omission counts inflate with non-unsafe content — an internal contradiction between the two layers of this surface.

## Defended / non-issues
- Empty CLI digest writes no alias (`sqlite.go:445`) — no CLI dedup, consistent with synchronous one-shot commands.
- Alias-conflict `Existing` results carry caller ctx without ownership — safe because no adapter executes on `Existing`.
- `payloadHash` concatenation cannot collide (unique sorted keys, `k=v\x00` framing); byte-truncation rune-splits are mirrored storage-side and JSON-safe.
- QA fence heartbeat after finish correctly fails `ErrStaleFence` (attempt outcome set, `lifecycle.go:38-55`); pre-finish `WithoutCancel` heartbeats work (test-pinned).
- `FinishOperation` flush failure corrupting outcome to `timed_out` needs a <5s finish context; all wired callers pass ≥30s — unreachable today.
- Cross-manager finish nil-op success is unreachable in wired topologies (one manager per serve/TUI session/CLI command).
- Trust boundary holds end-to-end: fingerprint stripped and recomputed server-side at prepare and again before execution (`operations.go:215,376-409`), token consumption binds session+canonical+fingerprint (`security.go:413-437`), digests derive only from server-side data.

# Review report: `product-state-mirror` (job `review-product-state-mirror-correctness`)

Verified at frozen commits (target `5d54525`, workspace `ab12dc38`). All four primary files read in full, plus routing sites (`study/state.go`, `sprint/state.go`, `sprint/execute_state.go`), validators, discovery, `runcontrol/sqlite.go` (DSN/permission comparison), `runcontrol/migration.go` (RestoreBackup), and repo-wide caller search (`productstate.` appears only in the three adapters + `storage_commands.go`). No test coverage exists for this surface (confirmed: `internal/productstate/` = store.go only; zero test references repo-wide), so all claims below were verified against live behavior using a binary built from the frozen tree into `/tmp/opencode` plus fixture workspaces — **the target tree and workspace were never modified**. Empirical demonstrations cited as [demo].

## Findings

### F1 — `Store.Load` is a non-atomic two-snapshot read; concurrent saves yield records that never existed — Severity: MEDIUM, Confidence: HIGH (mechanism probe-proven)
`Load` executes the header SELECT and the items SELECT as independent autocommit statements (`internal/productstate/store.go:129-147`) — no read transaction, no JOIN. In WAL mode each statement gets its own snapshot, so a Save committing between them tears the record: header from T1, item set from T2 (direction is always header-older/items-newer since header is read first). This contradicts the surface's own invariant ("readers see pre- or post-state per SQLite isolation", context pack §5, mirroring the single-tx writer guarantee at `store.go:154-205`).
Observable bad outcome [demo]: reader captured header `complete:false` (T1) while a committed save had deleted `task-2` (T2); the reassembled Record mixes both snapshots. Routed through the adapters, such a record passes `ValidateRunState` silently (nothing cross-checks header vs task set, `study/state.go:121-166`) and flows into status/resume/gate decisions as if authoritative; flow loads can serve stage payloads advanced past the header's Review/Smoke/QA evidence pointers, defeating the staleness gates those pointers drive. Trigger: any load concurrent with a save of the same record — multi-process access is an explicit design target (WAL + `_busy_timeout=5000` + `_txlock=immediate`, `store.go:67-73`; web server + CLI sharing one workspace). Counter-evidence searched: writers serialize among themselves via BEGIN IMMEDIATE, but nothing serializes readers against writers; no lock, retry, or version check exists on the read path.
Regression test: integration test holding a reader between Load's two statements (two `*sql.DB` handles, commit in between, as in the demo) asserting the returned Record equals one committed state exactly; today it can equal neither.

### F2 — `storage migrate --dry-run` writes DDL into an existing workspace database — Severity: LOW-MEDIUM, Confidence: HIGH (probe-proven)
The dry-run branch correctly skips `runcontrol.OpenSQLite` and `productstate.Ensure` (`internal/app/storage_commands.go:59-68`), but every record probe calls `Existing` → `open` → `createSchema` unconditionally (`store.go:41-51,79`, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` ×3). On a workspace whose DB predates the product tables, "preview" performs schema DDL.
Observable bad outcome [demo]: dropped `product_states`/`product_state_items` from a migrated workspace, ran `storage migrate --dry-run --json`, re-inspected `sqlite_master`: both tables (and the index) had been recreated by the dry run. Secondary effects: schema write locks taken against a possibly live server (a contended dry run surfaces SQLITE_BUSY as per-item `failed`/ExitPartial despite promising observation-only), and the operation mutates a production artifact the operator asked only to preview. Nuance stated honestly: the identical side effect occurs on the first load of any command via `Existing`, so this is systemic leniency of `open()` — but `--dry-run` is the one place whose contract is explicitly non-mutating ("Preview the migration", `docs/migration-product-state.md:6-9`). Dry-run on a workspace with NO DB correctly creates nothing ([demo]: `.ultraplan/` absent after run).
Regression test: runcontrol-only DB (product tables dropped) + `--dry-run` must leave `sqlite_master` unchanged; today it fails.

### F3 — Dry-run text summary reports would-imports as "imported" — Severity: LOW, Confidence: HIGH (probe-proven)
`appendItem` counts `"would_import"` into `result.Imported` (`storage_commands.go:72-74`), and the text summary prints that counter as imports (`storage_commands.go:134`). [Demo]: `storage migrate --dry-run` on three unmigrated artifacts prints item lines `would_import …` followed by `Product-state migration: 3 imported, 0 skipped, 0 failed`. The one mode whose purpose is preview claims completed imports in its summary; JSON mode is unaffected (carries `dry_run:true` + explicit statuses).
Regression test: text-mode dry-run summary must say `0 imported` / distinguish would-imports.

### F4 — A damaged authoritative row bricks the record permanently; shipped commands offer no repair and the valid checkpoint is ignored — Severity: LOW-MEDIUM, Confidence: HIGH (consequence chain probe-proven)
Authority is row-presence only (`store.go:41-51` stat + `Has`); loads are unconditional row-wins with no fallback (`study/state.go:27-35`, `sprint/state.go:20-32`, `execute_state.go:35-47`), and `header_hash`/`payload_hash` are written but never verified on any read path (`store.go:159-178` guards upserts only). Meanwhile `storage migrate`'s skip gate is also pure row-presence (`storage_commands.go:93-101` — `Has`, no content inspection), and no export/demote/reimport command exists.
Observable bad outcome [demo]: replaced the `study_run|alpha` header_json with valid-JSON-but-invalid content (missing timestamps) in the fixture DB; `study alpha status` then fails permanently with `run state malformed: … missing timestamps` while the on-disk checkpoint remained fully valid, and re-running `storage migrate` reports the broken record as `skipped`. Every future `LoadRunState` consumer (status/run-loop/resume) fails until manual sqlite surgery. Preconditions: byte corruption, partial external edit, or restore of a pre-migration backup (RestoreBackup swaps the whole file, `runcontrol/migration.go:293-352`, reverting product rows wholesale while post-backup file checkpoints — guaranteed stale under checkpoint gating — stay ignored). Fail-closed authority is defensible; the defect is the combination with zero integrity verification and zero shipped recovery path (doc promises only "Re-running the command skips records already in the database", `docs/migration-product-state.md:21-22` — which cannot repair). Primary ownership shared with run-journal-fencing for the restore leg.
Regression test: corrupt a stored header; `migrate` should classify it as failed (not skipped) or a documented verify/repair path must exist; today neither holds.

## Defended / non-issues
- **Silent sprint skip on `FlowStatePath` error** (`storage_commands.go:144-145,163-164` emit no item): unreachable for discovered sprints — discovery filters hidden/unsafe names (`project/discovery.go:40,75-85`), and `resolveSprintContained` is purely lexical containment (`workspace/paths.go` has no symlink resolution; `sprint/artifacts.go:55-75` always passes for names that survived discovery). Dead-guard asymmetry, not a reachable reporting hole.
- **Permissions of `Ensure`-created DB** (no runcontrol chmod/Lstat enforcement): empirically 0600 even under umask 022 [demo], matching runcontrol's enforced mode; residual difference is symlink-check only (security lens).
- **Special characters/spaces in workspace path breaking the DSN** (`url.URL` percent-encoding, `store.go:67-73`): verified end-to-end with a directory named `ws four#1` — import succeeds; driver percent-decodes correctly.
- **Duplicate item keys silently collapse last-wins in `Save`**: unreachable through product code — all three savers run domain validators that reject duplicate task IDs/stage names before any DB write (`study/state_database.go:46`, `sprint/state_database.go:75,105`).
- **DB rows bypass v1→v2 migration / pre-code-context interpretation**: impossible to store v1 — every saver validates current-schema only, and the import path migrates v1 in memory before persisting (`sprint/state.go:68-76`, `storage_commands.go:153-157`).
- **`updated_at` not bumped when only items change** (hash guard omits items, `store.go:160-166`): cosmetic; no code reads `updated_at`.
- **Per-record commit granularity / no global migration transaction**: matches the documented incremental-retry contract; crash leaves a prefix that rerun skips.
- **Concurrent Save+Save on one record**: serialized by `_txlock=immediate`; full-replace sweep sees prior committer's rows inside its own tx.
- **Cached-store stale-inode hazard after RestoreBackup rename** (process-lifetime cache, no Close, `store.go:39,84-89`): restore is documented offline-only ("Callers must stop all UltraPlan processes"); violation belongs to the fencing surface.
- **`studyWorkspaceRoot` derivation** (`filepath.Dir²` of `studies/<name>`): correct because `ResolveInside` normalizes lexically without symlink resolution, so `Study.Path` is always `<root>/studies/<name>`.
